entry.title: From Shared Ambition to Coordinated Collective Action

media:group.media:title: From Shared Ambition to Coordinated Collective Action
media:group.media:description:
Join us for a discussion on how governance can support coordinated collective action to transform shared ambitions into for social innovation and impact.
This panel discussion brings together social innovators, changemakers, and researchers to explore how governance can support coordinated collective action towards meaningful and lasting societal change. Drawing on practical experience and research insights, speakers dive into everything from transitioning from shared ambitions to coordinated action to designing evaluation and accountability frameworks that support learning and adjustment as projects and initiatives evolve.
About the Speakers:
• Dr. Adriane MacDonald Dr. Adriane MacDonald is an Associate Professor of Management and Canada Research Chair in Governance and Sustainability at the John Molson School of Business (JMSB). Dr. MacDonald is a multi-disciplinary researcher who focuses on understanding why business, government, and non-profit organizations partner to address sustainability issues; how partners communicate and collaborate; and how partnerships can be structured and managed to achieve tangible sustainability and corporate social responsibility outcomes. She is the principal investigator of the Carbon Governance Living Lab.
• David Guimont David Guimont is a partner at Si Lab and a recognized expert in the deployment of Living Labs. He supports organizations in designing co-creation processes and adopting more collaborative innovation practices. His recent work focuses on strengthening collective resilience to climate change and disasters. Between 2013 and 2024, he co-founded and co-directed the Laboratoire en Innovation Ouverte (LLio), a college centre for applied research, where he led numerous labs and people-centered design projects. A seasoned facilitator, he specializes in co-designing co-creation workshops and setting up innovation cells that foster experimentation in real-world conditions. Holding a master's degree in tourism planning and development from UQAM, he also works as an independent researcher and mentor to managers of social, territorial, and environmental impact projects.
• Michael Bossert Michael Bossert is Manager, Strategy, Innovation and Outreach at the Next-Generation Cities Institute. The development of inter- and transdisciplinary research is his focus, and he builds a global network dedicated to addressing urban challenges through Living Labs and Communities of Practice. He brings together stakeholders from governments, municipalities, the private sector, civic groups and academia to collaborate and boost city transformation. Since 2025 he started his journey as a PhD student in the Individualized PhD program at Concordia University Montreal. His research focuses on Metalabs and networks to collaborate and exchange knowledge based on case studies. His goal is to accelerate urban transformation and create impact in the Global North and South and improve strategies and policies.
• Juliette Champoux-Pellegrin Juliette is the second author on the Roadmap for Designing Living Lab Governance Structures, having spent the last year studying living lab initiatives and carbon governance. Her background is interdisciplinary, with eight years of experience working in social and private enterprises, nonprofit organizations, and research teams. With this experience, Juliette recently co-founded the nonprofit organization Montreal Climate Week and now serves as its executive director.
• Nilufar Sabet-Kassouf Nilufar Sabet-Kassouf (Nilu) has a multidisciplinary background, having studied in cell and molecular biology and biochemistry, and done research in neurophysiology at the intersection of music and meditation. For the past 7 years, she has shifted her focus to addressing complex socio-ecological challenges through her work at Future Earth and Sustainability in the Digital Age at Concordia University. In this capacity, she has been reflecting on the relationship between local realities and global priorities established through international science policy processes, and the role that technology plays in shaping these realities. More recently, Nilu has been leading the design and facilitation of capacity-building workshops and programs to cultivate ideas and practices of collective leadership and meaningful community engagement.

media:group.media:title: The Seven Shades of Resistance
media:group.media:description:
Resistance is often understood through visible acts of opposition, refusal, or confrontation. Yet it can also emerge through relationships, care, solidarity, responsibility, and the everyday negotiation of power.
The Seven Shades of Resistance invites a collective exploration of the relational dimensions of resistance: how it is shaped through our relationships with one another, communities, histories, and systems of power. The conversation will ask whose actions are recognized as resistance, whose remain unseen, and who holds the power to name resistance in the first place. It will also engage with the tensions and contradictions that arise when resistance is understood not only through what we stand against, but through the relationships we sustain, the responsibilities we carry, and the possibilities we create together.

entry.title: Accounting in the age of sustainability and artificial intelligence

media:group.media:title: Accounting in the age of sustainability and artificial intelligence
media:group.media:description:
Mark International Accounting Day by exploring the future of the accounting profession with a moderated panel discussion, followed by a networking reception.
Associate Dean of Graduate Programs Matthaeus Tekathen welcomes distinguished John Molson School alumni and industry leaders whose insights and experience will inspire and engage the next generation of accounting professionals. The evening will feature a moderated panel discussion, followed by networking.
This first-time event will spotlight emerging trends shaping industry and practice, with a focus on two themes; the evolving role of CPAs in advancing sustainable business practices and the potential for using artificial intelligence in the profession.
We hope you could join us to explore how we are redefining what counts—and how to count it!

media:group.media:title: Talking Shop: No Experience Necessary
media:group.media:description:
Join us at Concordia University's 4TH SPACE for Talking Shop, a live podcast recording from the Department of Marketing at the John Molson School of Business.
What does it really take to build a successful career and company even when you don’t have all the answers?
In this conversation, entrepreneur and Spin Master co-founder Ronnen Harary shares the story of his unconventional path, from his early experiences and first ventures to building global brands including PAW Patrol. We’ll explore uncertainty, failure, risk, timing and luck, why your 20s can be such an important period for experimentation, and how to recognize opportunities before they become obvious.
We’ll also talk about his book, No Experience Necessary, and the idea at its heart: you don’t necessarily need to have all the answers before you get started.
Hosted by Richard Sejean, marketer and lecturer at John Molson School of Business.

media:group.media:title: Film Festivals: Borders, Identities, Solidarities
media:group.media:description:
Launched at Ca’ Foscari University of Venice (UNIVE) in November 2024, the symposium Film Festivals: Borders, Identities, Solidarities continues in 2026 with its second edition at Concordia University in Montreal. Building on the discussions initiated in Venice, it aims to further explore how issues of borders, identities and solidarities have been shaped, negotiated and contested through film festivals in various contexts of social and political turbulences.
The symposium is organised around the idea that film festivals are highly visible cultural events, experienced by audiences in the present and documented for the future through catalogues, press materials, media coverage, and critical discourse. In the present, they act as political actors, shaping public engagement with and understanding of major societal issues of our past and present. This edition of the symposium places particular emphasis on film festivals as generators of wartime solidarity and war propaganda, as well as on the gendered dynamics of their engagement with conflict.
Knowing that wars profoundly affect societies and human lives, the ways in which they are interpreted, represented and remembered are particularly important. In this context, film festivals constitute valuable sites for examining how solidarities are mobilised, political positions articulated, and narratives of conflict legitimised, contested or transformed.

entry.title: The Fairy Creek Blockades and the Life Story of Pacheedaht Elder Bill Jones

media:group.media:title: The Fairy Creek Blockades and the Life Story of Pacheedaht Elder Bill Jones
media:group.media:description:
"I was lost before I was born": the starting point of Elder Bill Jones' lifelong journey of decolonization.
"You were all Indigenous once": the starting point for ending a world based on exploitation and greed.
We welcome Elder Bill Jones and Karen Moe, co-authors of the book Listening Once Again to Our Great Mother - The Fairy Creek Blockades and the Life Story of Pacheedaht Elder Bill Jones. The 2020-2021 Fairy Creek Blockades, against logging of an old-growth forest in BC, gathered First Nation people and settlers to become the largest act of civil disobedience in Canada. Elder Bill Jones recalls how, at the height of the resistance, he experienced the final phase of his awakening to the voice of the forest and the wisdom of his ancestors.
In conversation with Karen Moe, he will share essential teachings for our troubled time: about listening to the Earth, fighting to protect it, overcoming forces that fracture cultures and the self, and finding true dialogue beyond the colonial divide to face our collective fate. They will join virtually from BC, hosted by Nicolas Renaud, Associate Professor of First Peoples Studies, School of Community and Public Affairs, Concordia.

media:group.media:title: ARTE x CATs Research Commons
media:group.media:description:
Art Education and Creative Arts Therapies share methods, materials, knots, and emerging research.
The ARTE x CATs Research Commons is a one-day hybrid gathering bringing together faculty and students from Art Education and Creative Arts Therapies for an informal exchange of methods, materials, knots, and emerging research. Circulating between faculty roundtables, prompted exchanges, and student-led research-creation, the day invites participants to encounter what others are making, experimenting with, and working through.
The Research Commons offers an accessible and dynamic space for curiosity and unexpected points of overlap, where finding out takes precedence over expertise.

entry.title: Larissa Fassler in conversation with Nicole Burisch

media:group.media:title: Larissa Fassler in conversation with Nicole Burisch
media:group.media:description:
Moderated by Nicole Burisch, join us for a conversation around the conclusion of the research residency of Berlin-based artist Larissa Fassler. Since September, Fassler has been conducting on-site research, worked in Concordia’s archives, and explored Montréal as she developed a new drawing that maps the university’s architecture alongside the city’s student and political movements.
About the Speaker:
• Larissa Fassler Larissa Fassler (b. 1975, Vancouver) is a Berlin-based artist whose drawings, paintings, and sculptures map the emotional, political, and physical contours of urban life. Trained at Concordia University (BFA) and Goldsmiths, University of London (MFA), she walks and measures sites using her own body before translating fieldwork, overheard conversations and signage, and archival research into dense hand-drawn compositions that expose how power and memory shape public space. Solo exhibitions include the Musée d’Orsay (Paris); Kunsthalle Lingen (Germany); the Currier Museum of Art (Manchester, New Hampshire); the Esker Foundation (Calgary); and the Canadian Cultural Centre (Paris). Group shows include the Chicago Architecture Biennial and the São Paulo Architecture Biennial. Her work is held in the National Gallery of Canada, the Berlin State Museum, FRAC Nouvelle-Aquitaine MÉCA, and the Deutsche Bank Collection. Featured in Artforum, Frieze, Canadian Art, and The New York Times; monograph published by DISTANZ (2022). Represented by Galerie Poggi, Paris.
This event was organized by Prakash Krishnan
